fixtures.city_amends_note: Neither the city nor the regional code amends the counts. Section RBC306.2 adopts the Colorado Plumbing Code 'in its entirety', and the regional code deletes Chapter 29 of the International Building Code, so Table 403.1 of the plumbing code is the only fixture table. Colorado Springs Ordinance 23-16 (Appendix D) has no plumbing modification. The state pack's worked examples stand. The department lists the 2021 edition of the International Plumbing Code where the state pack read the 2024 edition; the rows used in the worked examples, Sections 403.1.1 and 403.2 (15 and 25 occupant exceptions) and Section 424.2 (urinal limits of 67 and 50 percent) were read in the 2021 edition and give the same numbers.
fixtures.table_quote: [Colorado Plumbing Code 2021 (IPC 2021) as shown on UpCodes, Table 403.1:] Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: water closets 1 per 75 male, 1 per 75 female. Business: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50. Educational facilities: 1 per 50. [403.1.1 exception:] Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. [403.2 exceptions:] Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. [...] Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. [...] Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets is provided in accordance with Section 405.3.4. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. [424.2:] In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
fixtures.confidence_note: The adoption without amendment was read in the department's own code PDF. The table and sections were read on UpCodes' copy of the Colorado Plumbing Code 2021 (the ICC's site blocks automated access).

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Colorado Springs job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the local building rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Colorado Springs offices, schools, churches and sports facilities, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** the building rules used in Colorado Springs require solid plastic (HDPE) used as an interior finish to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Colorado's plumbing rules, which Colorado Springs uses without changes, set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Colorado Springs extras:** in very large restrooms, the building rules used in Colorado Springs ask for 5% of the stalls to be wheelchair accessible, where federal law asks for at least one.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and the urinals are screened from the rest of the room. Colorado Springs adds no rule of its own. In buildings owned by the state, a state college, a county or a city, a new building or a renovated restroom must include an all-gender restroom; K-12 schools are outside that law. Colorado's civil rights rules allow separate men's and women's rooms and require that people may use the one that matches their gender identity.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Colorado Springs requires a permit to alter or repair a building and lists the work that needs none. The list covers painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, and movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department (719-327-2880) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department
page.stalls_after: These are the minimums for the whole building. Colorado Springs uses the state's counts as written and adds none of its own. An office that holds 25 people or fewer, or any space that holds 15 or fewer, does not need separate men's and women's rooms. A shared all-gender room is counted on everyone in the building instead of half.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules used in Colorado Springs count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department sets the final number.
skip_state_sources: Fire test for solid plastic partitions in public schools
page.install_rule: Colorado Springs permits and contractor licenses are handled by the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department. A contractor needs one of its licenses to do any work that requires a permit; ask the department which license class covers partition installation. Colorado doesn't license general or specialty contractors at the state level. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor doing work that needs a permit in Colorado Springs must hold a Pikes Peak Regional Building Department license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Colorado's wage law for public jobs covers state agency projects of $500,000 or more without federal money, at rates the state takes from the federal wage tables for the county; it does not cover city, county or school district projects. For a carpenter on building work in El Paso County the federal rate is $22.63 an hour plus $6.98 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.2% in Colorado Springs: 3.07% city, 2.9% state, 1.23% El Paso County and 1% Pikes Peak Rural Transportation Authority. Colorado Springs collects its own 3.07% under its own tax rules.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** installation labor listed separately on the bid, invoice or contract isn't taxed. Colorado Springs taxes an installation charge that is included in the price and not shown separately. A contractor owes the city's 3.07% on construction materials unless a tax-exempt organization buys them directly, and the state's exemption certificate for contractors covers only the taxes the state collects.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to Colorado Springs are taxable. Colorado Springs counts freight and delivery charges as part of the taxed price; the state taxes freight unless it is an optional charge shown on its own line. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it as use tax.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant, the City of Colorado Springs sales tax office (719-385-5903) or the Colorado Department of Revenue
page.buyers_extra: - **Sports venues and training centers:** HDPE or phenolic in locker rooms and shower areas, where water and heavy use are hard on stalls.
